x: There were some bright spots, particularly Simon Holmes' fine run in the 800m, but after the race an official from another club realised that we had run New Zealander Dennis Brown whose clearance to run in the league was apparently not due until a few days later.
As expected our new signing Dennis Brown soon took the lead followed by O'Hara, Jackson, Callow and Gorman. The rest of the 44 starters were soon strung out behind the leading runners.

Once again Dennis Brown showed his form with our fastest time of the day - 15:43. 'A' team: B.Gorman 16:49 (17th); L.Mann 17:13 (16th); S.Holmes 16:52 (15th); L.O'Hara 16:18 (13th); J.Rimmer 16:31 (13th); D.Brown 15:43 (10th).

Those who did compete ran encouragingly, particularly Dennis Brown who finished 11th of the 350 strong field - a great effort. Unfortunately he had no immediate back-up over the short, hilly five mile course until Simon Holmes in 87th place and Tony Binda in 93rd.

Laurie O'Hara led the team home in 4th just three places ahead of Dennis Brown. Simon Williamson was our 3rd scorer in 9th place, after some secret training in Birmingham and South Africa over the summer.

The deep snow was making the course very slippery and Dennis Brown was further hampered by heavy shoes. He gradually worked through though (encouraging the rest of the team as he went!) and finished just inside the first forty.

If only Laurie O'Hara and Jim Rimmer could have made it... if only Dennis Brown, who was there, was qualified to run.... if only John Bicourt could have finished (he was 17th last year) .... if only Simon Williamson, running well but for Birmingham University as an individual, had been on our team .…

Simon Williamson ran as well as could be hoped but such was the standard on the first stage that he handed over in 31st position and despite a fine run by Dennis Brown on the third stage our highest and final position was 27th.
Derek Crookes in the Southern Road Relay. Bearded Dennis Brown runs the Southern Road Relay.
Cliff Brooks in the shot, Derek Williams in the 200m, Dennis Brown in the 800, Reg Hopkins in the long jump, Peter Crosbie in the javelin and 4 x 100 relay team

In what was to be one of his last appearances before returning to his native New Zealand, Dennis Brown just managed to get the better of Laurie O'Hara by the narrowest of margins in this annual tussle to lead home the traditionally large field.
